Published online:
    August 31, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (primary focus: United States, with secondary focus on Europe, Japan, Middle East)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — recaps August month-end market moves
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — September Fed rate hike odds, ECB meeting Sept 9-10, payrolls report, CPI data Sept 11, BoJ potential hike
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    Markets sold off on Aug 31 as a U.S.-Iran military escalation drove oil sharply higher (Brent +2.71% to $90.49, WTI +2.83% to $85.76), reigniting inflation fears. Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech pushed September rate hike odds to 65% (from 35%), lifting 10Y Treasury yields to 4.758% — highest since Jan 2025. Equities fell across the board (Dow -0.70%, S&P -0.33%, Nasdaq -0.12%, STOXX 600 -0.60%) though all major indexes closed August with monthly gains. The dollar slipped despite rate hike expectations; the yen firmed on BoJ hike signals from Treasury Secretary Bessent. Key near-term catalysts: August payrolls (expected +58K after July's -23K shock) and September 11 CPI print.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US stock market pricing?
Relevance: YES — Core drivers are Fed rate hike trajectory, Treasury yields, geopolitical oil shock feeding into US inflation, and direct US equity index moves.

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: 72 — The U.S.-Iran military flare-up is a significant new/unexpected development. The hawkish Fed pivot from Warsh (a relatively new Chair) materially shifting September hike odds from 35% to 65% is also a notable surprise. Combined with a weak July payrolls print and elevated oil, the uncertainty stack is meaningfully above baseline.

Q03. Is the content explicitly about bullish impact on the US stock markets?
Explicit: NO — Monthly gains are noted but framed as residual, not forward-looking momentum.
Impact score: 8

Q04. Is the content explicitly about bearish impact on the US stock markets?
Explicit: YES — Rising yields, oil-driven inflation risk, hawkish Fed repricing, geopolitical escalation, and the seasonal September weakness narrative all point bearish.
Impact score: 68
